_about: How to make your own copy of a game, per console. Shown from each game's ROM slot and info panel. Links point to dumping.guide (a non-profit community wiki run by Hit Save!) and the official homebrew/emulator guides.

guides.title: Dumping an N64 cartridge
steps: Get a USB cartridge reader that supports N64 games. The Open Source Cartridge Reader is one; dumping.guide lists others.
Insert your cartridge and save it to your PC as a .z64 file.
Load it in Cartridge. It checks the dump is complete and the right version. .v64 and .n64 files are converted for you.

guides.title: Dumping a SNES cartridge
steps: Get a USB cartridge reader that supports SNES games (dumping.guide lists several).
Insert your cartridge and save it to your PC as a .sfc file.
Load it in Cartridge. It checks the dump and removes old copier headers if there are any.

guides.title: Dumping a NES or Famicom game
steps: Get a USB cartridge reader that supports NES/Famicom games (dumping.guide lists several).
Dump your cartridge to your PC as a .nes file.
Load it in Cartridge. It checks the dump against the No-Intro list.

guides.title: Dumping a Game Boy cartridge
steps: Get a USB Game Boy cartridge reader (dumping.guide lists several).
Dump your cartridge to your PC as a .gb or .gbc file. Most readers can back up your save too.
Load it in Cartridge.

guides.title: Dumping a Game Boy Advance cartridge
steps: Get a USB cartridge reader that supports GBA games (dumping.guide lists several).
Dump your cartridge to your PC as a .gba file.
Load it in Cartridge.

guides.title: Dumping a DS game
steps: Follow the DS guide on dumping.guide. It covers dumping with a cartridge reader or with your own console.
Save the game as a .nds file and load it in Cartridge.

guides.title: Dumping a 3DS game
steps: On your own 3DS with homebrew set up, use GodMode9 to dump the cartridge or an installed game.
Copy the .3ds file from your SD card's gm9/out folder to your PC and load it in Cartridge.

links.label: Dumping titles and cartridges (3DS Hacks Guide)

guides.title: Dumping a Virtual Boy cartridge
steps: Some cartridge readers support Virtual Boy with an adapter. See dumping.guide for the current options.
Save it as a .vb file and load it in Cartridge.

guides.title: Ripping a GameCube or Wii disc
steps: On a Wii (or a Wii U in Wii mode) with the Homebrew Channel, run CleanRip.
Rip your disc to an SD card or USB drive. Use NTFS, or let CleanRip split the file, because Wii discs are bigger than 4 GB.
Copy the .iso to your PC and load it in Cartridge. It reads the disc ID to check it's the right game and region.

guides.title: Dumping a Wii U game
steps: On your own Wii U with homebrew set up, dump the disc or installed game with the tools in the Wii U Hacks Guide.
Copy the dumped game folder to your PC and load it in Cartridge.

links.label: Dumping Wii U discs (Wii U Hacks Guide)

guides.title: Dumping a Sega cartridge
steps: Get a USB cartridge reader that supports your Sega system (dumping.guide lists several).
Dump your cartridge to your PC and load it in Cartridge.

guides.title: Ripping a Sega CD, Saturn or Dreamcast disc
steps: Follow the Sega disc guide on dumping.guide. Most need a PC disc drive and a ripping tool; Dreamcast discs need a special method.
Load the .cue, .gdi or .chd file in Cartridge.

guides.title: Ripping a game disc on your PC
steps: Put your disc in a PC disc drive (DVD drive for PS2) and rip it with a tool from the general disc guide on dumping.guide.
You get a .cue/.bin set or an .iso. Load it in Cartridge.

guides.title: Dumping a PS3 game
steps: Follow the Redump PS3 guide. It covers dumping with a compatible Blu-ray drive or your own console.
Load the dumped game folder in Cartridge.

guides.title: Dumping a PSP game
steps: Follow the Redump PSP guide to dump your UMD with your own PSP.
Load the .iso in Cartridge.

guides.title: Dumping a PS Vita game
steps: See the Sony section on dumping.guide for dumping Vita cartridges with your own console.
Load the dumped game folder in Cartridge.

guides.title: Dumping an Xbox or Xbox 360 disc
steps: Follow the Microsoft disc guide on dumping.guide.
Load the .iso in Cartridge.

guides.title: Dumping a PC Engine / TurboGrafx-16 card
steps: Get a cartridge reader that supports HuCards (dumping.guide lists options).
Dump it to a .pce file and load it in Cartridge.

fallback.title: Making a copy of your own game
steps: dumping.guide has step-by-step guides for most consoles, cartridges and discs, with the tools to use.
Load the file you make in Cartridge. It tells you whether it's the version the port needs.
